Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 25)
Topic: How Mantra Shakti Actually Works — Energy Sour ces, Aura Shielding, Chakras, and the Sukshma Sharir

Sour ce: A short Ashaeiynn Foundation training video (video transcript, ~19.5 min) — a dir ect instructional monologue rather than a live satsang Q&A, explicitly framed as part of a structur ed course on V edic-method mantra practice. Ends with "next video" rather than any live audience interaction. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this is a short, dir ect training monologue with no sangat back-and-forth — ther e is no separate curated conversational supplement for this session (see closing note).
1. WHY THIS TOPIC MATTERS

This session is intr oduced as foundational for a structur ed course on the Vedic method of mantra practice , explaining mechanically how mantra shakti (mantra power) actually operates: through which stages it moves, where it draws ener gy from, and how it gradually builds siddhi (spiritual accomplishment) in the body . The stated r eason for teaching the mechanism, rather than simply giving instructions to follow , is that once a practitioner's own drishti (spiritual sight) opens, they will need to r ecognize and interpr et these same pr ocesses for themselves — someone who already understands the mechanism will find the experience familiar rather than confusing, and those who have this knowledge have a responsibility to pass it on to others who haven't had the same opportunity to learn it.
2. THE BASELINE SOURCES OF ENERGY EVERY PERSON RECEIVES (EVEN WITHOUT ANY PRACTICE)

Even a person who does no jaap (chanting) or tapasya (austerity) at all still r eceives energy fr om at least two baseline sour ces. The first is external: food and water consumed by the physical body pr ovide physical str ength. The second baseline sour ce is brahmandiya urja (cosmic/universal energy). A simple illustrative example: if a person sleeps on an empty stomach and doesn't move all night, they still wake up with some ener gy — this energy could not have come fr om the act of sleeping itself, so it must come fr om somewher e else: cosmic energy falling continuously , like fine droplets of rain, onto every point of the earth, 24 hours a day . A specific detail fr om Bhaiya's own family's experience is offer ed: during a visit to "Y aksha Lok," the family learned that the sun's energy (per Surya Vigyan, "Sun Science") is diverted to Yaksha Lok, converted ther e, and then r eleased back onto the earth in the form of this cosmic/universal energy — and this is what nurtur es and sustains every living being ("shishu"). Simply sitting still and staying stationary in one place also allows this continuously falling cosmic ener gy to accumulate and compile within a person, even without any specific spiritual practice — this is of fered as an explanation for why some meditation centers instruct people to "just sit like this" to receive ener gy . Physical body energy ther efor e comes fr om external food; astral (sukshma) body energy comes fr om cosmic/universal energy — these two channels operate for every person regardless of whether they engage in any deliberate practice, though this
baseline is not the focus of this session.
3. THE THIRD SOURCE: A MANTRA-SPECIFIC "TARANG" (WAVE/CONNECTION) TO THE DEITY'S LOKA

Once a practitioner engages in the specific sadhna taught within Ashaeiynn Foundation — the practice thr ough which drishti will eventually open — a third, additional sour ce of energy becomes available beyond the two baseline sour ces: mantra shakti cr eates a tarang, a "wave" or tether, connecting the practitioner directly to the loka (r ealm) of the deity associated with the mantra being chanted. This tarang is described as a continuous energy sour ce connected dir ectly to that deity's r ealm — a genuinely new "wire" or connection, cutting thr ough the ambient cosmic energy , reaching all the way to the deity's loka. Once this tarang forms, it courses continuously thr ough the practitioner's body , becoming a third distinct sour ce of energy (alongside food-based physical ener gy and cosmic/universal astral ener gy).
4. THE FIRST STAGE: HOW MANTRA BUILDS AURA SHIELDING

When a practitioner begins mantra jaap, the mantra first begins to "sit" (settle) within the body . As this settling continues, the mantra gradually begins cir culating within the practitioner's aabhamandal (aura-field) — meaning it first establishes the surr ounding "envir onment," and only afterward does it become held within the body itself. As the mantra settles into the body , it gradually fills what this teaching calls the practitioner's 12 "quantum goles" (spheres) — referenced from an earlier training video — and filling these goles pr oduces thr ee protective shields ar ound the practitioner . Continued jaap beyond this point continues adding further shields (a fourth, fifth, sixth, and onward), and these shields gradually thicken into overlapping pr otective "plates" surr ounding the body .
5. THE SECOND STAGE: DEITY'S MESSENGERS EVALUATE ELIGIBILITY AND GRANT THE TARANG

After roughly five to six such shields have formed, a practitioner becomes eligible to r eceive the deity's tarang, or for doots (messengers/emissaries) fr om that deity's loka to arrive. These doots function somewhat like "commanding officers" arriving to assess the situation — they observe and evaluate whether the practitioner meets a specific eligibility criteria, which differs fr om person to person. If the doots judge the practitioner suitable, they grant the tarang r elatively quickly — this tarang is described as an actual tether or wire connecting the practitioner directly and continuously to that deity's loka, becoming a durable, ongoing new source of ener gy alongside the two baseline sources already available to everyone.
6. THE THIRD STAGE: THE TARANG STRIKES THE MULADHARA AND ACTIVATES THE CHAKRAS

At a specific point, this tarang strikes the practitioner's Muladhara (r oot chakra), and this strike activates the Muladhara with the tarang's own speed and energy . Once the Muladhara activates, the practitioner's other chakras begin to open in sequence. As each bond/chakra opens, doots and devtas fr om that deity's loka arrive and take hold of the practitioner's kundalini shakti, guiding it upward thr ough successive dimensions and then back down again — first dimension, then back to square one; second dimension, then back to square one; third dimension, back to square one; and so on. Through this r epeated cycle of rising and r eturning, the practitioner's overall "dimension level" gradually and steadily incr eases over time, with chakra-opening driving dimension-crossing in tandem.

As dimensions ar e crossed, the practitioner gains access to, and connection with, the specific powers/for ces present at each dimension — this is what produces an increasingly fine-grained sensitivity to subtle phenomena: noticing whether a particular presence or place carries a specific shakti, negativity , or positivity , and physical sensations like sudden cold (a mantra-specific sensation) or a heavy sensation on the head when a lar ger power draws near .
7. THE FOURTH STAGE: THE SUKSHMA SHARIR (SUBTLE BODY) DEVELOPS

This same activation pr ocess pr oduces a fourth simultaneous effect: the str engthening and activation of the sukshma sharir (subtle body), r eferenced earlier in this training series. As dimensions incr ease, the sukshma sharir's own aurashielding gr ows corr espondingly , the practitioner receives mor e of the deity's tarang, gains mor e energy , and their chakras open further — meaning the sukshma sharir's gr owth and the earlier three processes all r einfor ce one another . Because the sukshma sharir becomes pr ogr essively mor e active, a practitioner begins to feel small, specific sensations — subtle positivity or negativity , whether something or someone nearby is exerting pr essure or has "grabbed" at them — almost immediately and dir ectly , rather than r emaining unaffected like "stone."
8. ALL FOUR PROCESSES RUN IN PARALLEL, AND WHY MORE JAAP IS NEEDED AT THIS STAGE

These four processes — aura shielding, the deity-specific tarang, chakra/dimension activation, and sukshma sharir development — all occur simultaneously and continuously thr ough mantra practice, not sequentially in isolation. Since a single mantra's energy output must now be divided among four distinct, ongoing functions at once (body protection/shielding, energy delivery via the tarang, chakra activation, and sukshma sharir development), a practitioner needs to incr ease the volume of mantra jaap at this stage to adequately power all four functions together . Despite this mantra-driven activity , the two baseline energy sour ces (food for the physical body , cosmic/universal energy for the astral body) continue operating in parallel and ar e unaffected — they simply add to the total. When these multiple energy sour ces operate together , a practitioner becomes what this teaching calls a genuine "r eservoir" of energy — and that accumulated reservoir is itself what begins to attract or repel various forces and phenomena around the practitioner .
9. A CLOSER LOOK AT AURA SHIELDING: FROM PLATES TO A PROTECTIVE "GRID OF FIRE"

Returning to examine the aura-shielding pr ocess specifically in mor e depth: as mantra jaap continues, the body becomes pr ogr essively "cover ed" by the mantra, forming shields one after another . Once roughly 30 or mor e repetitions/r ounds of this shielding pr ocess accumulate, a cir cular arrangement of overlapping plates begins to form ar ound the practitioner . Beyond that point, a "grid" of fir e (agni) is pr oduced — a continuously cir culating field of mantra-fir e surrounding the practitioner , which negativity finds far mor e difficult to penetrate than in earlier stages. (Early on, before this grid fully forms, some negativity could potentially still slip in; once the grid is established, it can no longer penetrate. ) This grid of fire visually r esembles a flame, and this teaching offers it as the explanation for accounts or depictions of aghori sadhus and ascetics fr om whom fir e appears to emanate despite their thin, auster e physical bodies — this is presented as the visible sign of having crossed from plates into a fully-formed protective grid.
10. A CLOSER LOOK AT THE TARANG: WHY THE SAME MANTRA CAN LEAD DIFFERENT PEOPLE TO DIFFERENT DEITIES

Returning to examine the tarang specifically: the tarang eventually settles and establishes itself at a particular chakra, and this placement is determined by the practitioner's individual ishta devta (personally worshipped deity), not by the mantra's words alone. Each mantra is associated with a specific chakra and a specific deity in principle, but which particular deity actually appears for a given practitioner is decided by that practitioner's own individual ishta devta — the deity , not the practitioner , decides where within the body the tarang will settle. A concr ete illustration: if two people both chant the exact same mantra ("Jai Siya Ram," for example), one practitioner might find Hanuman Ji Maharaj manifesting behind them, while the other might find Bholenath (Lord Shiva) manifesting instead — because their individual ishta devtas differ . The chakra at which the tarang settles is specifically the chakra associated with that person's own ishta devta , and once settled, the tarang begins forming its own aabhamandal (localized aura) there, gradually taking on a rounded/spherical shape that, over time, develops into a siddhi (spiritual attainment/power). Eventually this accumulated form grows too lar ge to remain contained within the body and becomes externally visible/perceptible.
1 1. A CLOSER LOOK AT CHAKRAS AND DIMENSION-CROSSING

Returning to examine chakra-opening and dimension-cr ossing specifically: while mantra jaap continues, the deities associated with each opened chakra ar e simultaneously working to raise the practitioner's overall dimension. The kundalini shakti is r epeatedly taken up to a given dimension to r eceive knowledge specific to that dimension, then brought back down to a baseline ("squar e one"), then taken up to the next dimension, br ought back down again, and so on — through this repeated rising-and-returning cycle across each successive dimension, the practitioner's overall dimension gradually and steadily incr eases.
12. A CLOSER LOOK AT THE SUKSHMA SHARIR: THE PROGRESSION OF SUBTLE PERCEPTION

Returning to examine the sukshma sharir specifically: as the practitioner's dimension incr eases, the sukshma sharir gains pr ogr essively gr eater accessibility and capability to per ceive and understand subtle phenomena. A typical progr ession is described: initially a practitioner feels nothing at all; then mild sensation begins; then much str onger sensation; then actual sight (seeing) begins; then genuine knowledge/understanding arises; then intuition develops; then subtle hearing develops; and eventually deeper sight (drishti) develops. All of these successive r esults ar e described as manifesting specifically thr ough the sukshma sharir , and ar e felt/known essentially instantly and dir ectly ("as it is") — because the sukshma (astral) body and the sthula (physical) body ar e described as two sides of a single coin, functioning together at all times; whatever occurs in one will pr oduce an effect in the other . This direct, immediate correspondence between the two bodies is described as a natural "byproduct" of how they are linked.
13. ALL FOUR PROCESSES TOGETHER PRODUCE AN "UNMATCHED" LEVEL OF ENERGY

When aura shielding, the deity-specific tarang, chakra/dimension activation, and sukshma sharir development all operate together continuously , a practitioner's overall energy level becomes, in this teaching's words, genuinely unmatched/unparalleled ("achook").
14. A CAUTION: WHAT HAPPENS IF ENERGY IS DIVERTED ELSEWHERE

A caution is raised r egarding this entir e process: if, during this pr ocess, a practitioner diverts their own developing shakti toward some other purpose or destination, pr oblems can arise fr om that diversion. For now , however , this teaching frames the curr ent stage of practice as building a foundational structur e ("aap ek foundation build kar rahe hain") on which a practitioner can eventually genuinely "rule" ("raaj kar sakte hain") — with further detail on this diversion risk, and other topics, promised for the next video in this series.

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 25, English)
How Mantra Shakti Actually Works — Energy Sour ces, Aura Shielding, Chakras, and the Sukshma Sharir
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation training module. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Do I get any spiritual energy at all if I don't chant any mantra or do any practice? A: Jai Siya Ram! Yes — even without any jaap or tapasya, every person receives ener gy from two baseline sources: physical ener gy from food and water , and astral ener gy from brahmandiya urja (cosmic/universal ener gy), which falls continuously onto the earth like fine droplets of rain, 24 hours a day .

Q2. Where does that "cosmic energy" actually come fr om? A: Per an account from Bhaiya's own family's experience visiting "Yaksha Lok," the sun's ener gy (through Surya Vigyan, "Sun Science") is diverted there, converted, and released back onto the earth as this sustaining cosmic/universal ener gy that nurtures every living being.

Q3. If I just sit still without doing any specific practice, can I still gain energy? A: Yes — simply staying stationary in one place allows the continuously falling cosmic ener gy to accumulate and compile within you over time, even without deliberate spiritual practice. This is of fered as the explanation for why some meditation centers instruct people to "just sit like this" to receive ener gy .

Q4. Why is Bhaiya teaching us the technical mechanics of mantra instead of just telling us what to do? A: Because once a practitioner's own drishti (spiritual sight) opens, they will need to recognize and interpret these same processes for themselves. Someone who already understands the mechanism will find what they see familiar rather than confusing — and those who've had the opportunity to learn this have a responsibility to help others who haven't had the same chance.

Q5. What extra sour ce of energy do I get once I actually start Ashaeiynn's mantra sadhna? A: A third source appears beyond the two baseline ones: mantra shakti creates a "tarang" — a wave or tether — that connects you directly and continuously to the loka (realm) of the deity associated with your mantra. This becomes an ongoing ener gy source in its own right, alongside food-based physical ener gy and cosmic astral ener gy .

Q6. What actually happens in my body when I start doing mantra jaap? A: The mantra first begins to "sit" (settle) within your body , and as this continues it starts circulating within your aabhamandal (aura-field) — establishing the surrounding environment first, before becoming held within the body itself.

Q7. What ar e the "12 goles" mentioned in this teaching? A: They're referenced from an earlier training video as 12 "quantum spheres" within the practitioner's body . As mantra jaap continues, it gradually fills these goles, and filling them produces three protective shields around the practitioner — with more jaap adding further shields (a fourth, fifth, sixth, and beyond) that thicken into overlapping protective plates.

Q8. How do I know when I've r eached a stage wher e a deity actually starts paying attention to my practice? A: This teaching describes that after roughly five to six shields have formed, a practitioner becomes eligible for doots (messengers) from the relevant deity's loka to arrive and evaluate them, somewhat like commanding of ficers assessing whether the practitioner meets a specific eligibility criteria (which dif fers from person to person). If judged suitable, the tarang connection is granted relatively quickly .

Q9. What is the "Muladhara strike" mentioned in this teaching? A: At a specific point in practice, the tarang strikes the practitioner's Muladhara (root chakra), activating it with the tarang's own speed and ener gy . This activation then triggers the practitioner's other chakras to begin opening in sequence.

Q10. What happens to my kundalini shakti as my chakras open? A: Doots and devtas from the relevant deity's loka arrive as each chakra opens, and they guide the kundalini shakti upward through successive dimensions and then back down again repeatedly — first dimension then back to square one, second dimension then back to square one, and so on. Through this repeated cycle, the practitioner's overall dimension level gradually and steadily rises.

Q1 1. Why do I sometimes feel a sudden cold sensation, or a heaviness on my head, during practice? A: As dimensions are crossed, you gain access to and connection with the specific forces present at each dimension, producing increasingly fine-grained sensitivity to subtle phenomena. A sudden cold sensation is described as mantra-specific, while a heavy sensation on the head can occur when a lar ger power draws near .

Q12. What is the "sukshma sharir" and how does it r elate to all of this? A: The sukshma sharir (subtle body) strengthens and becomes more active as this whole process unfolds — its growth and the aura-shielding, tarang, and chakra/dimension processes all reinforce one another . As it becomes more active, a practitioner begins to feel small, specific sensations (subtle positivity , negativity , or pressure from something nearby) almost immediately , rather than remaining unaf fected.

Q13. Why do I need to incr ease how much mantra jaap I do as my practice deepens? A: Because at this stage, a single mantra's ener gy output is being divided simultaneously among four ongoing functions at once — aura shielding, the deity-specific tarang, chakra/dimension activation, and sukshma sharir development. To adequately power all four functions together , more volume of jaap is needed.

Q14. What does the "grid of fir e" ar ound some sadhus actually mean? A: This teaching explains that once roughly 30 or more rounds of accumulated aura-shielding form, a circular arrangement of overlapping plates develops, which then progresses into a continuously circulating "grid" of mantra-fire (agni) that negativity can no longer penetrate. This is of fered as the explanation for depictions of aghori sadhus and ascetics from whom fire appears to visibly emanate, despite their thin, austere physical bodies.

Q15. If two people chant the exact same mantra, will they experience the exact same deity? A: Not necessarily — the tarang settles at the chakra associated with each individual practitioner's own personal ishta devta (worshipped deity), not simply according to the mantra's literal words. For example, if two people both chant "Jai Siya Ram," one might find Hanuman Ji Maharaj manifesting behind them while the other finds Bholenath (Lord Shiva) instead, depending on their individual ishta devta.

Q16. What's the typical order in which spiritual per ception actually develops thr ough this practice? A: A typical progression described in this teaching is: no sensation at all, then mild sensation, then much stronger sensation, then actual sight, then genuine knowledge/understanding, then intuition, then subtle hearing, and eventually deeper drishti. All of these are described as manifesting through the sukshma sharir and being felt almost instantly , because the physical and astral bodies are tightly linked as two sides of one coin.

Q17. Is ther e any risk involved in building up all this energy thr ough practice? A: Yes — this teaching cautions that if a practitioner diverts their developing shakti toward some other purpose or destination during this process, problems can arise from that diversion. For now , though, the current stage of practice is framed as building a foundational structure that a practitioner can eventually "rule" upon, with more detail on this risk promised for a future video.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 25 additions)

When a user asks why they should learn the technical mechanics of mantra practice rather than just being given instructions, explain the stated reasoning: understanding the mechanism in advance helps a practitioner recognize and interpret their own

experiences once drishti opens, rather than being confused by them. When explaining ener gy sources, keep the three-tier structure clear: (1) food/water for the physical body , (2) cosmic/universal ener gy for the astral body (available to everyone), and (3) the mantra-specific tarang to a deity's loka (available only through dedicated sadhna) — don't collapse these into one undif ferentiated concept. If a user asks why they experience a specific deity through their mantra practice, use the ishta-devta framing from this session — the tarang settles according to the practitioner's own personal ishta devta, not simply the mantra's literal wording, so two people using the same mantra may have dif ferent experiences. If a user describes physical sensations during practice (cold, heaviness, sudden feelings), validate these as consistent with this teaching's described progression, without overstating or diagnosing what specific power or presence is involved. Do not overstate what has been taught on the risk of "diverting shakti elsewhere" — this session explicitly defers detailed explanation of that risk to a future video. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
